definitions.explanation: A vivid, deep red color. Originally referred to the dye extracted from safflower (紅花). A literary and poetic word for red.

examples.japanese: {夕焼|ゆうや}けが{空|そら}を{紅|くれない}に{染|そ}めた。
examples.english: The sunset dyed the sky crimson.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると、{山|やま}の{木々|きぎ}が{紅|くれない}に{色|いろ}づき、{美|うつく}しい{風景|ふうけい}が{広|ひろ}がる。
examples.english: In autumn, the mountain trees turn crimson, creating a beautiful landscape.

notes:
A literary and elegant word for a deep, vivid red. The character {紅|くれない} can also be read as べに (lipstick, rouge) — a separate entry — but くれない specifically refers to the color itself with a poetic nuance.

ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from the dye produced from {紅花|べにばな} (safflower), which was historically imported via China. The word くれない is thought to come from {呉|くれ}の{藍|あい} (indigo/dye from the kingdom of Wu), referring to the Chinese origin of the dyeing technique.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紅|くれない}に{染|そ}まる: to turn crimson
- {紅|くれない}に{色|いろ}づく: to take on a crimson hue
- {紅|くれない}の{涙|なみだ}: crimson tears (literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赤|あか}: red — the everyday, general-purpose word for red
- べに ({紅|べに}): rouge, lipstick — the cosmetic reading of the same character
- {緋|ひ}: scarlet — a brighter, more orange-tinged red
